sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who asks, what job does the bot do, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: States the user and the job in one sentence
Derives questions per day and peak questions per second from 25,000 a month
Names a success metric with a baseline and target, gated on zero permission leaks
Lists what is out of scope (for example Slack Connect, actions, excluded folders)

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the system as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Has a layer that resolves the Slack user into source-system principals
Shows sync of both content and permissions
States that permission filtering happens in code, not in the prompt

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: For each source, what is indexed, how are its permissions modelled, and how do changes arrive?
criteria: Describes the permission model of each of Confluence, Drive and Jira
Names a change feed per source (webhook or change API) plus a reconciliation job
Keeps excluded folders out at the connector so they are never fetched
Handles link-shared Drive files without treating them as public

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How do documents become chunks that carry their context and permissions, and how do edits flow?
criteria: States a chunk size and splitting rule
Adds title or breadcrumb context to each chunk before embedding
Updates only changed chunks by hash, with tombstones for deletes
Estimates embedding cost for a full build and for daily churn

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: What is the control flow from question to answer, and what bounds it?
criteria: Rewrites thread follow-ups into a standalone query
Caps searches and wall-clock time with numbers
Skips generation and abstains when retrieval scores are below a threshold

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the bot remember, where, and for how long?
criteria: Uses the Slack thread as conversation memory rather than a separate copy
Caches principals with an expiry shorter than the revocation SLA
Re-runs retrieval with the new asker's permissions when someone else follows up in a thread

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Which tools exist, and how do they enforce permissions?
criteria: Lists each tool with its arguments
Derives principals from the caller identity, never from a tool argument
Avoids leaking titles of forbidden documents in errors
Handles concurrent token refresh (single-flight or equivalent)

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: How does the bot meet Slack's 3-second rule, and where does the latency go?
criteria: Acks before doing any retrieval or model work
Dedupes Slack retries by event id
Gives a latency table by stage whose total fits the 4 s first-text target
Throttles message edits to Slack's rate limits

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached, what is not, and what does a question cost?
criteria: Shows per-question and monthly cost with and without prompt caching
Keeps every permission-related cache under the 15-minute revocation SLA
Rejects a shared answer cache across users because of permissions

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Where do chunks, vectors and ACLs live, how big are they, and how does a filtered query run?
criteria: Sizes the vector storage from chunk count and dimensions
Applies the ACL filter inside the retrieval query (pre-filter), not after top-k
Combines keyword and vector search (for example RRF) with a rerank step
Adds a live permission check on final candidates

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does an answer look like, and how does it differ between a DM and a channel?
criteria: Includes linked sources with last-updated dates
Restricts channel answers to documents every channel member can see
Collects feedback on every answer

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: For each rule protecting data or trust, what enforces it if the model ignores its instructions?
criteria: Enforces document permissions and channel mode in code
Checks each answer sentence against its cited chunk and abstains when support is low
Blocks external or guest users by Slack attributes
Runs a permission probe set that fails CI on any leak

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: What number moves, and how do you prove the bot moved it?
criteria: Gives baseline and target for the headline metric
Uses a holdout (channels or users with the bot off)
Measures retrieval quality offline with a labelled set (recall@k)
Converts the result into hours or dollars

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what catches each failure?
criteria: Covers a stale ACL after revocation
Covers missed webhooks with reconciliation
Fails closed when a permission check errors or times out
Covers a model provider outage with a fallback

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds the labelled question set and permission probes first
Ships one source with correct ACLs before adding more
Ends each step with a measurable number
